blocks.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions. Write True or False for the true-false questions.

stimulus.text:
It was raining hard on Monday morning. Aarav stood at the bus stop with his mother. He held a big blue umbrella. Six other children stood in a line. Nobody pushed or shouted. They all waited for the number 12 bus.

A small girl at the end of the line had no umbrella. Her bag was getting wet. Aarav stepped closer and held his umbrella over her. “Thank you,” she said, and smiled. Her name was Diya.

Soon the bus came with its lights on. The driver opened the door. The children got in one by one. Aarav found a window seat. Diya sat next to him. The rain drummed on the roof all the way to school.

items.q: Who was with Aarav at the bus stop?
items.answer: his mother

items.q: Which bus were the children waiting for?
items.answer: The number 12 bus

items.q: What did Aarav do for Diya?
items.answer: He held his umbrella over her
options: He held his umbrella over her
He bought her a new umbrella

items.q: Why did Aarav hold his umbrella over Diya?
items.answer: Diya had no umbrella (1 mark), and her bag was getting wet (1 mark).

items.q: Write two things the children did at the bus stop or on the bus to show good manners.
items.answer: Any two: they stood in a line; nobody pushed or shouted; they got in the bus one by one (1 mark each).

answerPoints.point: First correct thing from the passage
Second correct thing from the passage

items.skill: reading: two points from two places

items.q: Aarav had no umbrella.
items.answer: False. He held a big blue umbrella.

items.q: Diya sat next to Aarav on the bus.
items.answer: True

items.q: What colour was Aarav’s umbrella?
items.answer: blue

items.q: On which day of the week did the story happen?
items.answer: Monday

items.q: What was the small girl’s name?
items.answer: Diya

items.q: Who opened the door of the bus?
items.answer: the driver

blocks.instruction: Read the note and answer the questions. Write True or False for the true-false questions.

stimulus.text:
A note from Amma
Please be careful in the kitchen. There is some water on the floor near the sink. Wipe it up at once, or you may slip. Keep the rice and the sugar in closed boxes. Put the milk in the fridge. Four chairs stand near the stove. Push them back to the wall. The hot pan can burn your hand, so do not touch it. Call an adult if you need help.

items.q: Where is there some water, and why must you wipe it up?
items.answer: The water is on the floor near the sink (1 mark). You must wipe it up so that nobody slips (1 mark).

answerPoints.point: On the floor near the sink
So that you do not slip

items.q: Where should the rice and the sugar be kept? Where should the milk be put?
items.answer: The rice and the sugar should be kept in closed boxes (1 mark). The milk should be put in the fridge (1 mark).

answerPoints.point: Rice and sugar: in closed boxes

items.q: Write two things in the note that can hurt a person. Say how each one can hurt.
items.answer: The water on the floor can make you slip (1 mark). The hot pan can burn your hand (1 mark).

answerPoints.point: Water on the floor, and you may slip
Hot pan, and it can burn your hand

items.skill: reading: two-part answer from two places

items.q: There is some water near the _____.
items.answer: sink

items.q: If you need help, call an _____.
items.answer: adult

items.q: The four chairs must be pushed back to the _____.
items.answer: wall

items.q: The water is on the kitchen table.
items.answer: False. It is on the floor.

items.q: Four chairs stand near the stove.
items.answer: True

items.q: Who wrote the note?
items.answer: Amma

blocks.instruction: Give a short answer to each question.

items.q: Who wrote the letter to the children?
items.answer: the traffic police

items.q: Name the two colours of a zebra crossing.
items.answer: black and white

items.q: Which rule is called “Be Alert”? Write its number.
items.answer: Rule 6

blocks.instruction: Answer the following questions in full sentences.

items.q: Why did the traffic police write the letter to the children?
items.answer: They wrote to share simple safety tips with the children (1 mark), so that the children stay safe on the roads and help keep the roads accident-free (1 mark).

answerPoints.point: To share safety tips / rules with the children
So that the children stay safe on the roads (or the roads stay accident-free)

items.skill: textual: purpose of the letter, two places in the text

items.q: How do the children reach school, according to the letter? Write any two ways.
items.answer: Any two: on foot; by bicycle; by bus (1 mark each).

items.q: What should you stick on your clothes when you walk on a road in the evening? How does it help?
items.answer: Reflective stickers (1 mark). They help the drivers to see you clearly (1 mark).

items.q: Where are traffic lights installed? Which colour must the pedestrian signal show before you cross?
items.answer: Traffic lights are installed on very busy roads (1 mark). You must wait for the pedestrian signal to turn green (1 mark).

items.q: What would you do if your friend asked you to run across a busy road just for fun? Give a reason.
items.answer: Model answer: I would say no and walk with my friend to the zebra crossing, because a car or a bus may come suddenly and hurt us. (Any sensible action and a sensible reason.)

answerPoints.point: A sensible action, for example: say no, tell a grown-up, use the zebra crossing
A reason that mentions danger, vehicles or an accident

items.markingGuide: Think and discuss. A sensible action (says no, calls the friend back, tells a grown-up, uses the zebra crossing) — 1; a reason about danger, vehicles or accidents — 1. An action with no reason — 1. Maximum 2.

blocks.instruction: Write five sentences. Choose one topic.

items.q: Write five sentences about the road near your school. You can say what you see, what you hear and how you stay safe there. OR Write five sentences about the way you come to school every day.
items.answer: Model answer: The road near my school is very busy. I see buses, cars and bicycles there. I hear many horns. I use the zebra crossing to cross the road. I walk on the footpath and hold my father’s hand.

answerPoints.point: Sentence 1: clear and on the topic
Sentence 2: clear and on the topic
Sentence 3: clear and on the topic
Sentence 4: clear and on the topic
Sentence 5: clear and on the topic

items.markingGuide: One mark for each clear sentence on the chosen topic, five sentences in all — 5. A sentence that is off the topic or has no verb — 0 for that sentence. Deduct 1 for more than three spelling errors. Never go below 0. Maximum 5.

blocks.instruction: Write a letter of thanks. Follow the four steps.

items.q: Write a short thank-you letter to the traffic police. Follow the four steps. Step 1: Begin with “Dear Officer,” and say who you are (your name and class). Step 2: Thank the police for one thing they do for children. Step 3: Write one road-safety rule you have learnt. Step 4: Promise one thing you will do, and end with “Yours sincerely,” and your name.
items.answer: Model letter: Dear Officer, I am Riya of Class 4. Thank you for helping us cross the busy road near our school. I have learnt that we must walk on the footpath. I promise that I will always use the zebra crossing. Yours sincerely, Riya

answerPoints.point: Step 1: opens with Dear Officer and says who the writer is
Step 2: thanks the police for one thing
Step 4: makes one promise and closes with Yours sincerely and a name

items.markingGuide: One mark for each of the four steps done in full sentences — 4; a step that is missing or unclear — 0 for that step. Deduct 1 for more than three spelling errors. Never go below 0. Maximum 4.

blocks.instruction: Make a sentence of your own with each word.

items.q: Make a sentence with the word “alert”.
items.answer: Model answer: A good pedestrian stays alert near the road.
items.markingGuide: A sentence that uses the word correctly and makes sense — 1; the word missing, or used wrongly — 0. Ignore one small spelling slip. Maximum 1.

items.q: Make a sentence with the word “careful”.
items.answer: Model answer: Be careful when you cross the road.
items.markingGuide: A sentence that uses the word correctly and makes sense — 1; the word missing, or used wrongly — 0. Ignore one small spelling slip. Maximum 1.

items.q: Make a sentence with the word “accident”.
items.answer: Model answer: The driver stopped in time, so there was no accident.
items.markingGuide: A sentence that uses the word correctly and makes sense — 1; the word missing, or used wrongly — 0. Ignore one small spelling slip. Maximum 1.

blocks.instruction: Fill in each blank with the word countable or uncountable.

items.q: The noun “helmets” is _____.
items.answer: countable

items.q: The noun “sand” is _____.
items.answer: uncountable

items.q: The noun “books” is _____.
items.answer: countable

items.q: The noun “air” is _____.
items.answer: uncountable

items.q: The noun “milk” is _____.
items.answer: uncountable

items.q: Meena added some sugar to the halwa. Rewrite the sentence with “three spoons of” in place of “some”.
items.answer: Meena added three spoons of sugar to the halwa.

answerPoints.point: The rest of the sentence is unchanged and correct

items.skill: grammar: make an uncountable noun countable

items.q: Aman ate two bowls of rice and drank two bottles of milk. Rewrite the sentence with “some” in place of both counting phrases.
items.answer: Aman ate some rice and drank some milk.

items.q: Sam drank three waters. Rewrite the sentence correctly.
items.answer: Sam drank three bottles of water. (Also correct: three glasses / cups / jugs of water, or Sam drank some water, or Sam drank water.)

answerPoints.point: Water is not counted directly: a counting word before “of water”, or “some water”
The rest of the sentence is correct and complete

items.q: Write the countable noun and the uncountable noun in this sentence. Cows drink water.
items.answer: Countable noun: cows. Uncountable noun: water.

items.q: Write these words in two lists, Countable and Uncountable: pencils, rice, cars, sugar, chairs, sand.
items.answer: Countable: pencils, cars, chairs. Uncountable: rice, sugar, sand.

items.q: Write a counting phrase for each noun. Use a number and a container word, for example “two jugs of water”. (a) sand (b) sugar
items.answer: Model answer: (a) two buckets of sand (b) three spoons of sugar. Also correct: bags, heaps, handfuls, trucks of sand; bags, packets, cups, kilos, spoons of sugar.

answerPoints.point: A number and a container word before “of sand”
A number and a container word before “of sugar”

items.q: Write two sentences. Use a countable noun from the box in one sentence and an uncountable noun from the box in the other. Box: buses, milk, pencils, sand
items.answer: Model answer: Two buses stopped at the school gate. The children played in the sand.

answerPoints.point: A correct sentence with buses or pencils
A correct sentence with milk or sand

items.markingGuide: One sentence with a countable noun from the box (buses or pencils), used correctly — 1; one sentence with an uncountable noun from the box (milk or sand), not made plural — 1. Maximum 2.

blocks.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

items.q: Match the words with their meanings.
items.answer: pedestrian – a person who goes on foot; footpath – a path beside the road for people to walk on; reflective – able to shine back light so that it can be seen; distract – to take your attention away from something; zebra crossing – a marked place on the road for people to cross

pairs.right: a person who goes on foot
a path beside the road for people to walk on
able to shine back light so that it can be seen
to take your attention away from something
a marked place on the road for people to cross

blocks.instruction: Write the following lines in neat handwriting.

stimulus.text: On Sundays, Baba and I ride our bicycles to the park. I wear my helmet and ring my bell at every turn. We stop to drink water under a big banyan tree.

items.q: Copy the lines in your best handwriting.
items.answer: A neat, evenly spaced copy with the capital letters, commas and full stops in place.
items.markingGuide: Letters well formed — 1; even spacing between letters and words — 1; neat writing with correct capital letters and punctuation — 1. Maximum 3.

blocks.instruction: Write the following lines in neat handwriting.

stimulus.text: Our class has a small garden near the gate. “Please water the plants,” says Miss Rao. We fill our mugs and walk slowly.

items.q: Copy the lines in your best handwriting.
items.answer: A neat, evenly spaced copy with the speech marks, comma and full stops in place.
items.markingGuide: Letters well formed — 1; even spacing between letters and words — 1; neat writing with correct capital letters, speech marks and punctuation — 1. Maximum 3.
